An entry here clears exactly ONE recorded demotion attempt from the exit code. It never
hides it: an acknowledged event is still printed in full on every fire, tagged with the
Matching is by IDENTITY, not by class: at + origin + repaired SET + bodyFieldCount must
all match. A new attempt from the same writer doing the same thing has a different `at`
`fixCommit` must be an ANCESTOR OF THE COMMIT THE SERVICE IS SERVING. If a deploy rolls
the fix back, the ack goes VOID and the event alarms again. If ancestry cannot be
determined (no git, unknown sha, no serving commit), the ack does NOT apply -- fail closed.
Do not add an entry for an attempt you have not root-caused and fixed. `issue` must name a
settled issue and `fixCommit` the commit that made a recurrence impossible by that path.
Attribution alone ('we know who did it') is NOT grounds for an ack.
